messages:
Maria: Heads-up — during last night's 6h locust replay we saw a steady increase in idle DB connections and a few pgbouncer errors (no available clients). Did anyone else catch this in their dashboards? :eyes:

Ajay: Yep spotted the same. pg_pool_in_use climbed to 100% around hour 4, connections never dropped. CPU and IO look fine.

Maria: Pasted a small snippet from the replay app logs and pgbouncer: ```
2026-04-12T03:45:12Z ERROR db: connection leak suspected, stacktrace truncated
2026-04-12T03:45:13Z pgbouncer FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser
2026-04-12T03:45:13Z app WARN: failed to get client from pool: timeout after 30s
--- locust summary ---
Requests: 1.2M, Failures: 412 (0.03%), Median latency 135ms
```

Tim: Looks like a leak + exhaustion rather than a blunt surge. Any recent PRs touching the DB client / kv-cache paths?

Sam: @Maria tagging FYI — I opened PR #432 yesterday which changes how we reuse connections in the kv-cache fallback. It includes an explicit client.release() in the error path but I didn't include it in the earlier canary. Could be related. :thinking_face:

Nina: If it's leaking on exceptions then a slow steady climb matches. Can we correlate request traces to see which endpoint is holding clients?

Ajay: I can add a short trace to the replay to pin the few endpoints that spike connection wait time. Will run a 30m focused run against the failing scenario.

sre-bot: ALERT: pgbouncer_pool_exhausted on cluster-redwood-prod-db-1 during replay-2026-04-12. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/pgbouncer-exhaustion :warning:

Tim: Quick mitigations we can do now: 1) bump pgbouncer pool size by +20% (fast but memory cost), 2) lower app DB pool_max from 50->40 to avoid overcommit, 3) deploy PR #432 to close leak. Prefer sequence 3 then 1 if we need immediate headroom.

Maria: I'm leaning to deploy PR #432 to canary first (it fixes explicit release), then run the focused 30m locust to validate. If still high, bump pool. I'll kick off canary now.

Sam: Thanks — linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/service/pull/432 (contains tests + change log). I added a small unit test that simulates error path but not full soak coverage.

Ajay: Starting 30m focused replay against canary in ~5m, will post metrics. Test scenario: 800 RPS steady, same user mix that caused leak.

Nina: Also add a short Grafana alert for connection_wait > 100ms for >2m so we catch regressions sooner. I can push that dash change.

Maria: Great. If the canary looks good we can roll to nightly soak. If not, we'll revert and do pool bump. Scheduling a quick sync: tomorrow 10:00am PST (15m) to triage results.

Tim: :thumbsup: ping me if it starts failing; I'll stand by to apply pool bump and rollback if needed.

Ajay: Focused run started: 1835556900. Will update with graphs in ~35m.

Maria: Thanks team — appreciate the quick coordination.

Sam: FYI I also added extra logging around connection open/close in the PR, should help root cause if it reproduces.

sre-bot: NOTE: If escalation needed, follow DB-oncall rota in #eng-oncall.
